description: The national quality indicators are Norway's official set of measures of how well health services perform, from municipal care to hospitals, ambulances and mental health services. They are compiled and published by Helsedirektoratet, the Norwegian Directorate of Health, for patients, service managers and authorities. Indicators are grouped into municipal health services, dental services, prehospital services, somatic hospital care and mental health, and are shown by municipality, county, health region, health trust or hospital. New figures are published four times a year, with most indicators updated annually, and each indicator has an article describing its definition and caveats. An export view lets users download the indicator database free as Excel or CSV, dashboards compare municipalities or hospitals, and the Directorate's content is also available through its open HAPI API. Caveats: the export runs in a Power BI view, not as static files, indicator definitions and caveats must be read one by one, and no licence is named on the pages read. Simulation uses: setting performance baselines such as prehospital response and hospital quality measures for healthcare and emergency service models, and comparing regions before and after disruptions. Related records: the Finnish Sotkanet indicator bank (data-sotkanet-indicator-bank) and the CIHI indicator library (data-cihi-indicator-library-and-data-tables) are comparable national indicator sources.
